mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS below 0.5%) compresses the risk-free rate, reducing the discount rate for equity valuations and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6.0% over the past 3 months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically precede a decline in corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods where UNRATE exceeds 6.0%, or the Rank IC over 2-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous surge in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) combined with a contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a supply-constrained economy that triggers inflation fears and monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods where HOUST and RSAFS are above their 1-year moving averages and INDPRO is below its 1-year moving average, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS rising above 4.5% for 3 consecutive months), the S&P 500 typically experiences negative forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to increased discount rates and reduced risk appetite.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods during a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for 3 months), or the Rank IC over 2-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) over the past 6 months signals improving labor market conditions, which typically lead to higher consumer spending and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where UNRATE has declined for 6 consecutive months, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A housing starts (HOUST) above 1700 thousand units signals strong consumer demand for housing, which typically precedes a rise in consumer spending and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where HOUST exceeds 1700, or the Rank IC over 2-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime (INDPRO > 110 and UNRATE < 5.0%), the S&P 500 typically experiences positive forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to strong economic growth and corporate earnings momentum.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods during a late-cycle expansion (INDPRO > 110 and UNRATE < 5.0%), or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A retail sales (RSAFS) above 550,000 million dollars signals strong consumer spending, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where RSAFS exceeds 550,000, or the Rank IC over 2-year rolling windows is below 0.03.
